Hi all,

We're very excited to announce Statlib (https://stat-lib.github.io), a project to lay the foundations for formalized mathematical statistics.

Mathematical statistics is the discipline that brings rigor to the cutting-edge methods of modern data analysis. Moreover, it draws on multiple fields — real, functional, complex, and convex analysis, measure theory, stochastic calculus, and information theory, among others. Yet the statistics- and probability-related APIs in Mathlib remain sparse compared to other areas of mathematics. Statlib aims to close that gap, and, in doing so, to create new mathematical abstractions from statistical theory; in this process, we also hope to contribute relevant math theory to Mathlib.

Beyond the code, we have a community goal: to build the language of statistics together with statisticians and Lean experts. For us, formalization is a community craft — shared design decisions, open discussion of architecture, and a culture of careful, responsible review. We've seeded the library with initial contributions to the abstract framework of statistical risk that underpins so much of the field, and we maintain a projects page where researchers can propose, contribute to, and grow specific areas — developing the core of the library along the way.

We look forward to your questions, comments, and suggestions, and to many exciting and constructive discussions ahead.

We are very excited to announce the Statlib channel #Statlib ! -- Please Subscribe!!

Statlib is a community for building the practices, shared vocabulary, and reusable Lean infrastructure needed to develop theoretical statistics in formal language. We hope this channel will be a place where statisticians, Lean contributors, students, and researchers from related fields can propose ideas, ask questions, coordinate projects, and help the library grow in ways that benefit both statistical research and the broader Lean ecosystem.

We expect the channel to serve several related purposes -- please refer to https://stat-lib.github.io/contribute.html for precise details.

(i) It will serve as a discussion space for ongoing Statlib work: questions about definitions, proofs, architecture, style, documentation, review, and how different projects should fit together. 

(ii) The channel will be a place to propose topics and research questions in mathematical statistics and possible working groups.

(iii) We plan to use the channel for regular office hours and community check-ins. These can include updates from ongoing projects and working groups, help with Lean coding practices, discussions of reviews, questions about style and documentation, and shared architectural decisions arising from active work.

(vi) We hope the channel will welcome and connect Lean experts with the mathematical statistics community. We will use it to share workshops, tutorials, events, reading groups, and opportunities to learn more about Lean 4, Mathlib, Statlib, and ongoing formalization efforts.

We look forward to building Statlib together through open discussion, careful contributions, and a shared commitment to making formalized statistics useful, readable, and research-driven. Look forward to a future of exciting discussions and growing together!
